content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-19
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-19
14	
15	- Q: `POST /chat/sessions` accepts an optional `title`, the backend has no auto-titling logic of its own, and no endpoint exists to rename a session afterward — so whatever the app does at creation time is permanent for that conversation. Should the app send a title derived from the first message, or never send one? → A: The app derives a short title client-side from the first message's text (trimmed, capped to a short preview length) and sends it in `POST /chat/sessions`'s `title` field at the moment that first message creates the session. This is the only mechanism that can ever give a conversation a human-recognizable name, and User Story 4 explicitly requires the side menu to let users find past conversations "by name." (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16	- Q: `GET /chat/sessions` is cursor-paginated (`cursor`/`limit`, default 20, max 50) and its items carry no documented sort order; the prototype's side-menu extract shows a flat "CONVERSAS" list with no load-more control. How should the side menu order and page through sessions once an account has more than one page's worth? → A: The list is ordered by most recent activity (`lastUserMessageAt`, descending; a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed, since sessions are only created together with their first message), and the side menu fetches further pages via `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the "CONVERSAS" section (the same infinite-scroll pattern already established for RF07's own list) — so no conversation ever becomes unreachable as the account accumulates sessions beyond a single page. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
17	- Q: `docs/input/requirements.md` §6.3 marks both `GET /chat/sessions` and `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` as "works offline (cache)," without scoping that to only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped. Does offline mode cover every previously-opened conversation, or only the one open at disconnect? → A: The cache (and offline readability) covers every chat session the user has opened at least once while online — both the side menu's own session list and the message history of each previously-opened conversation remain browsable and switchable while offline; only creating a session, sending a message, and retrying require connectivity (already covered by FR-012). Selecting a conversation from the side menu that was never loaded while online, while currently offline, shows the standard no-connection state (no cached data to fall back to) rather than any content. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (Priority: P1)
22	
23	A user opens the chat and asks the AI agent something related to their life, without repeating what they already wrote elsewhere. The agent's answer reflects relevant things the user recorded before, not just the current message in isolation, and the exchange stays on screen as a normal, persisted conversation the user can come back to.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF04 — "memory" via semantic search over past entries. Without it, the screen is just a generic chat window with no connection to the rest of the product.
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding an account with a prior entry about a specific topic, sending a chat message that references that topic without quoting it verbatim, and confirming the agent's response demonstrates awareness of the seeded entry's content.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** the user has at least one prior entry about a specific topic, **When** they send a chat message related to that topic, **Then** the agent's response reflects information from that entry, even though the message itself never restated it.
32	2. **Given** a conversation already has one or more exchanges, **When** the user leaves the screen and returns later (including after an app restart), **Then** the full exchange history is still present, in the same order, without needing to be resent.
33	3. **Given** the user sends a chat message, **When** the message is accepted, **Then** it is stored and displayed as part of the conversation but does **not** create a journal entry — chat messages are conversational only, with no automatic persistence as an entry (the one exception, an explicit save action, belongs to a later unit and is out of scope here).
34	
35	---
36	
37	### User Story 2 - Always knowing what the agent is doing (Priority: P1)
38	
39	While waiting for or reading a response, the user can always tell, at a glance, which of three things is happening: the answer is still arriving, it finished successfully, or it failed — and a response that stops arriving partway through never just vanishes.
40	
41	**Why this priority**: RF04's acceptance criteria explicitly require these three states and the no-disappearing-partial-message rule; without a clear, honest status, users cannot trust the chat enough to rely on it.
42	
43	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by sending a message and observing the UI progress through the "processing/streaming" state into either "complete response" or "error," and separately by forcing a connection drop mid-response and confirming the partial text stays visible with a failure indication instead of disappearing.
44	
45	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
46	
47	1. **Given** the user has just sent a message, **When** the agent begins producing a reply, **Then** the response is revealed progressively (streaming) with a visible in-progress indicator, distinct from a finished message.
48	2. **Given** a response finishes streaming normally, **When** the last token arrives, **Then** the message is shown in its final, complete form with its timestamp, no longer carrying any in-progress indicator.
49	3. **Given** the connection drops, or the backend returns an error, while a response is still arriving, **When** that happens, **Then** whatever text had already arrived stays visible, together with a clear failure indication in place of the timestamp — the message is never removed or left in an ambiguous unfinished-looking state.
50	
51	---
52	
53	### User Story 3 - Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (Priority: P2)
54	
55	A response fails or is cut short. The user taps the failed message and gets a fresh attempt at an answer to the same question, without having to retype it, without creating a duplicate question in the history, and without disturbing the rest of the conversation.
56	
57	**Why this priority**: A direct extension of Story 2's failure state — the failure indication is only useful if there's a documented way out of it, and the requirement calls this out explicitly ("a way to try again" is part of RF04's own scope).
58	
59	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a response failure, tapping the failed message to retry, and confirming a new response is generated for the same original question, with the user's question appearing exactly once in the history.
60	
61	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
62	
63	1. **Given** a message shows the "Falha ao gerar resposta" state, **When** the user taps it, **Then** a new response attempt starts for that same original question, going through the same processing/streaming → complete/error states as a normal response.
64	2. **Given** a retry is in progress or has completed, **When** the history is inspected, **Then** the user's original question appears exactly once — retrying never duplicates the question, only replaces the failed answer with a new attempt.
65	3. **Given** the retry itself fails again, **When** that happens, **Then** the message returns to the same failure state with the same way to try again — retrying is not limited to a single attempt.
66	
67	---
68	
69	### User Story 4 - Organizing conversations from the side menu (Priority: P2)
70	
71	A user wants to start a brand-new conversation without losing an existing one, and wants to see and return to past conversations by name and recency from the side menu.
72	
73	**Why this priority**: RF04's own scope explicitly includes the side menu's session list and "Novo Chat" action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4) — without it, a user has no way to manage more than one conversation at a time.
74	
75	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by having at least one existing conversation, opening the side menu, confirming it lists past sessions with a title and timestamp, tapping "Novo Chat," confirming the chat screen shows an empty conversation, and confirming the prior conversation is unchanged when reopened from the list.
76	
77	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
78	
79	1. **Given** the user has one or more existing conversations, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** a "CONVERSAS" section lists each one with a title and a timestamp.
80	2. **Given** the side menu is open, **When** the user taps the new-conversation action ("Novo Chat"), **Then** the chat screen shows an empty conversation, ready to accept a first message, without discarding any previous conversation.
81	3. **Given** the user selects a past conversation from the list, **When** it opens, **Then** its full message history is shown exactly as it was left.
82	
83	---
84	
85	### User Story 5 - Reading history while offline (Priority: P3)
86	
87	A user without a connection can still read everything they already loaded, but cannot send anything new, and is told clearly why.
88	
89	**Why this priority**: Explicitly one of the four required prototype states for this screen, and it protects against the worse failure mode of a chat screen that looks broken or loses content when connectivity drops — but it is a secondary concern relative to the core conversation and failure-recovery loops above.
90	
91	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a conversation, simulating a loss of connectivity, confirming the existing history stays visible and scrollable, confirming the send control is disabled with an explanatory banner, and confirming sending is not possible until connectivity returns.
92	
93	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
94	
95	1. **Given** a conversation is already loaded, **When** the device goes offline, **Then** the existing message history remains visible and scrollable, and a banner explains that new messages are blocked.
96	2. **Given** the device is offline, **When** the user looks at the composer, **Then** the send control is visibly disabled — no message can be sent until the connection returns.
97	3. **Given** the connection returns, **When** the user resumes using the screen, **Then** the send control re-enables and new messages can be sent normally.
98	4. **Given** the user has previously opened more than one conversation while online, **When** the device goes offline and the user switches between those previously-opened conversations from the side menu, **Then** each one's cached history is shown exactly as it was left, not just the conversation open at the moment connectivity dropped.
99	
100	---
101	
102	### Edge Cases
103	
104	- The user tries to send an empty or whitespace-only message: the send control stays disabled/inactive, and no request is made.
105	- A message at or near the backend's maximum length is sent: the system either prevents exceeding that maximum before sending or surfaces the backend's resulting validation error clearly, without losing the text the user typed.
106	- A message is sent while a previous response in the same conversation is still streaming, or is sitting in the failed/"tap to retry" state: the composer stays disabled until that turn resolves (completes or is retried to a new resolution), so a session never has two responses racing at once.
107	- The session expires (RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" behavior) while a response is mid-stream or while viewing history: the existing overlay is shown, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and once the user re-authenticates, the conversation resumes exactly where it was — this unit reuses that behavior rather than redefining it.
108	- The user navigates away from a conversation (e.g., via the side menu) while a response is still streaming: when the user returns to that conversation, the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded for it (complete or failed) rather than being stuck in a stale in-progress state tied to a connection that no longer exists.
109	- An account has zero conversations yet (first-ever use of chat): the chat screen still shows a ready-to-use empty conversation, and a session is created at the point the first message is actually sent.
110	- The user retries a failed message that is not the most recent message in the conversation: the retry still succeeds and only affects that specific message's response, leaving every later message in the conversation untouched.
111	- An account has more conversations than fit in one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` (more than its default/max `limit`): scrolling to the bottom of the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section fetches the next page via `cursor` rather than silently stopping at the first page.
112	- The user is offline and selects, from the side menu, a conversation that was never opened while online: no cached data exists for it, so the screen shows the standard no-connection state instead of any content, distinct from the normal offline case of browsing an already-cached conversation.
113	- Opening the side menu's conversation list, the export job, dashboard, filters, action-plan board, and every other screen or action not named in this feature's scope: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.
114

118

123	- **FR-005**: If the response stream is interrupted before completion (connection drop, backend error, or any other cause), the system MUST keep whatever partial text had already arrived visible, together with the failure indication — it MUST NOT remove, hide, or blank out a partial message.
124	- **FR-006**: A message in the error state MUST be tappable to trigger a retry (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`) that regenerates the response to that same original question. 128	- **FR-010**: A new conversation (`POST /chat/sessions`) MUST only be created at the point a first message is actually sent into an empty conversation state — opening an empty conversation state (via "Novo Chat," or on an account with no conversations yet) MUST NOT by itself create a session with no messages in it. 130	- **FR-012**: The system MUST NOT attempt to create a new conversation or send/retry a message while offline — both actions require a connection and MUST be blocked client-side rather than attempted and failed.
131	- **FR-013**: The screen MUST reuse the existing session-expiration handling (RF03/RF07's "Sessão expirada" overlay: history and scroll position preserved, re-authentication returning to the same conversation state) rather than introducing a separate expiration treatment for chat.
132	- **FR-014**: This unit MUST NOT implement the "save message as entry" button (RF10), the proactive-insight card (RF08), AI-persona selection as an active setting (extension, requirements section 2 — persona is only read at session creation as whatever the backend already returns), or any change to the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
133	
134	### Key Entities
135	
136	- **Chat Session**: One conversation thread, identified by an id, with a title derived client-side from its first message at creation time and shown in the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section (a defensive generic placeholder is shown only if a session is ever encountered with an empty title), the persona that was in effect when it was created (read-only here — not user-editable in this unit), and timestamps including when it was created and when it last received a user message (the latter drives the side menu's ordering).
137	- **Chat Message**: One turn inside a Chat Session — either the user's question or the agent's response — with its content, its position in the conversation, and its status (still arriving, complete, or failed). 138	- **Context used for a response**: The set of the user's own prior entries the agent draws on to ground a given response. 139	
140	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
141	
142	### Measurable Outcomes
143	
144	- **SC-001**: When a seeded prior entry exists on a topic, a chat message about that topic that does not restate the entry's content still produces a response reflecting that entry's information, in 100% of tested cases.
145	- **SC-002**: Every sent or retried message ends in exactly one of the three defined states (streaming → complete, or streaming → error) with zero cases observed stuck in an undefined or ambiguous state.

# Feature Specification: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Feature Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-19

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-19

- Q: `POST /chat/sessions` accepts an optional `title`, the backend has no auto-titling logic of its own, and no endpoint exists to rename a session afterward — so whatever the app does at creation time is permanent for that conversation. Should the app send a title derived from the first message, or never send one? → A: The app derives a short title client-side from the first message's text (trimmed, capped to a short preview length) and sends it in `POST /chat/sessions`'s `title` field at the moment that first message creates the session. This is the only mechanism that can ever give a conversation a human-recognizable name, and User Story 4 explicitly requires the side menu to let users find past conversations "by name." (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: `GET /chat/sessions` is cursor-paginated (`cursor`/`limit`, default 20, max 50) and its items carry no documented sort order; the prototype's side-menu extract shows a flat "CONVERSAS" list with no load-more control. How should the side menu order and page through sessions once an account has more than one page's worth? → A: The list is ordered by most recent activity (`lastUserMessageAt`, descending; a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed, since sessions are only created together with their first message), and the side menu fetches further pages via `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the "CONVERSAS" section (the same infinite-scroll pattern already established for RF07's own list) — so no conversation ever becomes unreachable as the account accumulates sessions beyond a single page. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: `docs/input/requirements.md` §6.3 marks both `GET /chat/sessions` and `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` as "works offline (cache)," without scoping that to only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped. Does offline mode cover every previously-opened conversation, or only the one open at disconnect? → A: The cache (and offline readability) covers every chat session the user has opened at least once while online — both the side menu's own session list and the message history of each previously-opened conversation remain browsable and switchable while offline; only creating a session, sending a message, and retrying require connectivity (already covered by FR-012). Selecting a conversation from the side menu that was never loaded while online, while currently offline, shows the standard no-connection state (no cached data to fall back to) rather than any content. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (Priority: P1)

A user opens the chat and asks the AI agent something related to their life, without repeating what they already wrote elsewhere. The agent's answer reflects relevant things the user recorded before, not just the current message in isolation, and the exchange stays on screen as a normal, persisted conversation the user can come back to.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF04 — "memory" via semantic search over past entries. Without it, the screen is just a generic chat window with no connection to the rest of the product.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding an account with a prior entry about a specific topic, sending a chat message that references that topic without quoting it verbatim, and confirming the agent's response demonstrates awareness of the seeded entry's content.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has at least one prior entry about a specific topic, **When** they send a chat message related to that topic, **Then** the agent's response reflects information from that entry, even though the message itself never restated it.
2. **Given** a conversation already has one or more exchanges, **When** the user leaves the screen and returns later (including after an app restart), **Then** the full exchange history is still present, in the same order, without needing to be resent.
3. **Given** the user sends a chat message, **When** the message is accepted, **Then** it is stored and displayed as part of the conversation but does **not** create a journal entry — chat messages are conversational only, with no automatic persistence as an entry (the one exception, an explicit save action, belongs to a later unit and is out of scope here).

---

### User Story 2 - Always knowing what the agent is doing (Priority: P1)

While waiting for or reading a response, the user can always tell, at a glance, which of three things is happening: the answer is still arriving, it finished successfully, or it failed — and a response that stops arriving partway through never just vanishes.

**Why this priority**: RF04's acceptance criteria explicitly require these three states and the no-disappearing-partial-message rule; without a clear, honest status, users cannot trust the chat enough to rely on it.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by sending a message and observing the UI progress through the "processing/streaming" state into either "complete response" or "error," and separately by forcing a connection drop mid-response and confirming the partial text stays visible with a failure indication instead of disappearing.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has just sent a message, **When** the agent begins producing a reply, **Then** the response is revealed progressively (streaming) with a visible in-progress indicator, distinct from a finished message.
2. **Given** a response finishes streaming normally, **When** the last token arrives, **Then** the message is shown in its final, complete form with its timestamp, no longer carrying any in-progress indicator.
3. **Given** the connection drops, or the backend returns an error, while a response is still arriving, **When** that happens, **Then** whatever text had already arrived stays visible, together with a clear failure indication in place of the timestamp — the message is never removed or left in an ambiguous unfinished-looking state.

---

### User Story 3 - Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (Priority: P2)

**Why this priority**: A direct extension of Story 2's failure state — the failure indication is only useful if there's a documented way out of it, and the requirement calls this out explicitly ("a way to try again" is part of RF04's own scope).

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a response failure, tapping the failed message to retry, and confirming a new response is generated for the same original question, with the user's question appearing exactly once in the history.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

3. **Given** the retry itself fails again, **When** that happens, **Then** the message returns to the same failure state with the same way to try again — retrying is not limited to a single attempt.

---

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has one or more existing conversations, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** a "CONVERSAS" section lists each one with a title and a timestamp.
2. **Given** the side menu is open, **When** the user taps the new-conversation action ("Novo Chat"), **Then** the chat screen shows an empty conversation, ready to accept a first message, without discarding any previous conversation.
3. **Given** the user selects a past conversation from the list, **When** it opens, **Then** its full message history is shown exactly as it was left.

---

A user without a connection can still read everything they already loaded, but cannot send anything new, and is told clearly why.

**Why this priority**: Explicitly one of the four required prototype states for this screen, and it protects against the worse failure mode of a chat screen that looks broken or loses content when connectivity drops — but it is a secondary concern relative to the core conversation and failure-recovery loops above.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a conversation, simulating a loss of connectivity, confirming the existing history stays visible and scrollable, confirming the send control is disabled with an explanatory banner, and confirming sending is not possible until connectivity returns.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

2. **Given** the device is offline, **When** the user looks at the composer, **Then** the send control is visibly disabled — no message can be sent until the connection returns.
3. **Given** the connection returns, **When** the user resumes using the screen, **Then** the send control re-enables and new messages can be sent normally.
4. **Given** the user has previously opened more than one conversation while online, **When** the device goes offline and the user switches between those previously-opened conversations from the side menu, **Then** each one's cached history is shown exactly as it was left, not just the conversation open at the moment connectivity dropped.

- The user tries to send an empty or whitespace-only message: the send control stays disabled/inactive, and no request is made.

48	layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
49	returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
155	| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
156	| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |
157	
158	**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).
159	
160	### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
161	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
164	| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
165	| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
166	| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |
167	
168	**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.
169	
170	### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
171	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
174	| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
175	| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
176	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
177	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
178	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
179	| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
180	
181	### 6.4 Search
182	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
183	|---|---|---|
184	| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |
185	
186	### 6.5 Export
187	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
188	|---|---|---|
189	| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
190	| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
191	| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |
192	
193	### 6.6 Dashboard
194	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
197	| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
198	
199	### 6.7 Account
200	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
203	| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |
204

320	| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
321	|---|---|---|

323	| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
324	| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
325	| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
326	| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
327	| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |

333	## 11. Error codes (RNF09)
334	
335	Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:
336	
337	| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
338	|---|---|---|
339	| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
340	| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
341	| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
342	| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
343	| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
344	| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
345	| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
346	| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
347	| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
348	| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

350	The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.
351	
352	---
353	
354	## 12. Delivery order
355	
356	Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:
357	
358	**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

360	- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
361	- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.
362	
363	---
364	
365	## 13. Technical constraints
366	
367	**Fixed:**
368	- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
369	- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
370	- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
371	- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
372	- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
373	- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
374	- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
375	- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
376	- Folder convention:
377	
378	```
379	lib/
380	  core/
381	  features/
382	    <feature>/
383	      data/
384	      domain/
385	      presentation/
386	```
387	
388	**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

### 6.4 Search
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

### 6.5 Export
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |

### 6.6 Dashboard
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |

### 6.7 Account
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

---

## 7. Integrated flowchart — screens × requirements × backend

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph T0["Screen 0 — Splash"]
        direction TB
        E01["GET /auth/session"]
    end

    subgraph T01["Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault · RF03"]
        direction TB
        E02b["Face ID / Touch ID / PIN — validated on the device, no backend call"]
        E02["POST /auth/login (if the session has fully expired)"]
    end

    subgraph T1["Screen 1 — Home (chat) · RF04, RF08, RF10"]
        direction TB
        E04["POST /chat/sessions"]
        E05["GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages"]
        E06["POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages"]
        E06b["POST .../messages/:userMessageId/retry"]
        E07["POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight"]
        E07b["POST /entries (save message)"]
    end

    subgraph T2["Screen 2 — Insertion modal · RF01, RF02"]
        direction TB
        E08["POST /media/ocr"]
        E09["POST /entries"]
    end

    subgraph T3["Screen 3 — Side menu"]
        direction TB
        E10["GET /chat/sessions"]
        E10b["'Novo Chat' button — opens T1 empty, backed by E04"]
    end

    subgraph T4["Screen 4 — My records · RF05, RF06, RF07"]
        direction TB
        E11["GET /entries (source/dateFrom/dateTo — no category)"]
        E12["GET /entries/search"]
        E15["POST /export/summary"]
        E15b["GET /export/:jobId/status"]
        E16["GET /export/:jobId/download"]
    end

    subgraph T5["Screen 5 — Action plans (extension)"]
        direction TB
        E17["No calls — static"]
    end

    subgraph T6["Screen 6 — Settings · RF09, RNF05"]
        direction TB
        E18["GET /dashboard/aggregate"]
        E19["GET /dashboard/narrative"]
        E20["PATCH /account/settings"]
        E21["DELETE /account"]
        E22["POST /auth/logout"]
    end

    T0 --> T01 --> T1
    T1 --> T2
    T1 --> T3
    T3 -->|Novo Chat| T1
    T3 --> T4
    T3 --> T5
    T3 --> T6

    style T5 fill:#FAEEDA,stroke:#BA7517,color:#412402
```

*(The amber "Action plans" subgraph marks the only screen with no backend calls — a product extension.)*

---

## 8. Data model (reference)

Main entities of the backend (Supabase / Postgres). Field names are reference suggestions, not mandatory character by character. **Where this table differs from the API contract (`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`), the contract prevails** (see section 6).

| Table | Main fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | id, email, biometric_enabled, persona, created_at | RLS: a user accesses only their own row |
| `entries` | id, user_id, content, source (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), chat_message_id (nullable), embedding (vector, see 9), sync_status, created_at, updated_at | `embedding` generated in `POST /entries` via Voyage AI |
| `tags` | id, user_id, name | Extension — created manually by the user |
| `entry_tags` | entry_id, tag_id | N:N join table |
| `chat_sessions` | id, user_id, title, created_at | — |
| `chat_messages` | id, session_id, role (`user`/`assistant`), content, created_at | User messages show the RF10 button |
| `export_jobs` | id, user_id, status (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`error`), period_start, period_end, file_url, created_at | Asynchronous — see 6.5 |

**RLS pattern (every table with `user_id`):** policy `auth.uid() = user_id`, no exceptions.

---

## 9. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Mobile app | Flutter, BLoC, Clean Architecture |
| Backend | Already built and frozen; consumed through its API |
| Infrastructure | Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Storage + Auth + RLS) |
| Chat / vision / OCR / summary / insights / dashboard / PII | Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (the rest) — in the backend |
| Embeddings (RAG) | Voyage AI `voyage-4` — in the backend |
| Speech-to-text (audio transcription) | Whisper on-device (`whisper_ggml`); audio never reaches the backend |
| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |
| Layer rule | RNF06 |
| Test coverage | RNF07 |

---

## 10. Configuration parameters

Fixed values — not to be reinterpreted.

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

3	import 'package:cerne/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart';
4	import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
5	
6	/// On-device, cross-restart persistence for the entries the user has
7	/// already seen (the PRD's "local read cache" — requirements.md line 50/125:
8	/// results from it stay visible offline and reconcile with the server on
9	/// reconnect, with no duplicates). Keychain-backed, same pattern as
10	/// `VaultSecureStorage` — journal content is personal data, so it stays
11	/// encrypted at rest like the PIN it already sits behind.
12	///
13	/// Distinct from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s in-memory `cachedEntries`: that
14	/// field only ever held optimistic just-created entries for this process's
15	/// lifetime (research.md R8, 003-multimodal-capture). This class is what
16	/// makes that same list survive an app restart, which is what a cold open
17	/// on an already-offline device needs (closing snapshot at unit completion
18	/// did not cover this path — see Meus Registros intervention report).
19	class EntriesLocalCache {
20	  EntriesLocalCache({FlutterSecureStorage? storage})
21	    : _storage = storage ?? const FlutterSecureStorage();
22	
23	  final FlutterSecureStorage _storage;
24	
25	  static const _key = 'entriesLocalCache';
26	
27	  Future<List<Entry>> readAll() async {
28	    final raw = await _storage.read(key: _key);
29	    if (raw == null) return const [];
30	    try {
31	      final decoded = jsonDecode(raw) as List<dynamic>;
32	      return decoded.map((e) => _fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList();
33	    } on FormatException {
34	      return const [];
35	    } on TypeError {
36	      return const [];
37	    }
38	  }
39	
40	  Future<void> writeAll(List<Entry> entries) {
41	    final encoded = jsonEncode(entries.map(_toJson).toList());
42	    return _storage.write(key: _key, value: encoded);
43	  }
44	
45	  Map<String, dynamic> _toJson(Entry e) => {
46	    'id': e.id,
47	    'content': e.content,
48	    'source': e.source.name,
49	    'chatMessageId': e.chatMessageId,
50	    'occurredAt': e.occurredAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
51	    'tags': [
52	      for (final tag in e.tags) {'id': tag.id, 'name': tag.name},
53	    ],
54	    'piiStatus': e.piiStatus.name,
55	    'piiSpans': [
56	      for (final span in e.piiSpans)
57	        {'start': span.start, 'end': span.end, 'type': span.type},
58	    ],
59	    'embeddingStatus': e.embeddingStatus.name,
60	    'mediaDurationSeconds': e.mediaDurationSeconds,
61	    'serverRevision': e.serverRevision,
62	    'createdAt': e.createdAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
63	    'updatedAt': e.updatedAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
64	    'similarity': e.similarity,
65	  };
66	
67	  Entry _fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> data) => Entry(
68	    id: data['id'] as String,
69	    content: data['content'] as String,
70	    source: EntrySource.values.byName(data['source'] as String),
71	    chatMessageId: data['chatMessageId'] as String?,
72	    occurredAt: DateTime.parse(data['occurredAt'] as String),
73	    tags: (data['tags'] as List<dynamic>)
74	        .map(
75	          (t) => EntryTag(
76	            id: (t as Map<String, dynamic>)['id'] as String,
77	            name: t['name'] as String,
78	          ),
79	        )
80	        .toList(),
81	    piiStatus: PiiStatus.values.byName(data['piiStatus'] as String),
82	    piiSpans: (data['piiSpans'] as List<dynamic>)
83	        .map(
84	          (s) => PiiSpan(
85	            start: (s as Map<String, dynamic>)['start'] as int,
86	            end: s['end'] as int,
87	            type: s['type'] as String,
88	          ),
89	        )
90	        .toList(),
91	    embeddingStatus: EmbeddingStatus.values.byName(
92	      data['embeddingStatus'] as String,
93	    ),
94	    mediaDurationSeconds: data['mediaDurationSeconds'] as int?,
95	    serverRevision: data['serverRevision'] as int,
96	    createdAt: DateTime.parse(data['createdAt'] as String),
97	    updatedAt: DateTime.parse(data['updatedAt'] as String),
98	    similarity: (data['similarity'] as num?)?.toDouble(),
99	  );
100	}

1	# Implementation Plan: P-RF06 — Semantic search / filter
2	
3	**Branch**: `006-semantic-search-filter` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
4	extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)
5	
6	**Date**: 2026-10-17 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
7	
8	**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/006-semantic-search-filter/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
9	§1 (RF06), §6.4 (`GET /entries/search`), §6.2 (`GET /entries`), §8, §9, §10 (300 ms debounce), §13;
10	`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/entries` and `/entries/search` schemas; `docs/input/backend/fixtures/
11	seeded-search-entries.md`; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.4 ("Tela 4 — Meus Registros", "Sheet
12	de filtro", "Filtros ativos"); and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on RF07
13	(`specs/005-multi-source-timeline/`), already implemented — this is the unit that makes RF07's own inert
14	search bar and funnel button on "Meus Registros" actually do something.
15	
16	## Summary
17	
18	"Meus Registros" gains a live semantic search bar (`GET /entries/search`'s `q`, 300 ms debounced) and a filter
19	sheet (date-range + entry-type, mapped to `GET /entries`'/`GET /entries/search`'s shared `dateFrom`/`dateTo`/
20	`source` parameters), both narrowing the same `RecordsLoaded` list RF07 already renders. No new screen, no new
21	bloc: the already-built `RecordsBloc` is extended in place with six new events (`SearchTextChanged`,
22	`FilterSheetApplied`, `FilterChipRemoved`, `FiltersAndSearchCleared`, `CriteriaLoadRetried`, and an internal
23	`SearchDebounceElapsed`) and five new `RecordsLoaded` fields (the currently-applied
24	`searchQuery`/`dateRange`/`entryTypes`, plus `isApplyingCriteria`/`criteriaLoadFailure`), because
25	the two things RF06 must guarantee — "a new action supersedes any in-flight earlier one" (FR-005a) and "AND
26	across axes, OR within the entry-type axis" (FR-005) — both need a single, already-serialized owner of
27	"what the current criteria is and which fetch is the latest one," which is exactly what one bloc already is.
28	`EntriesRepository.list()` gains optional `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`limit` parameters (additive, RF07's own
29	cursor-pagination callers unaffected) and gains a new `search()` method (`GET /entries/search`, bounded,
30	no cursor — FR-005b). Multi-select entry types (`source` is single-valued; FR-003/FR-005's resolved
31	Clarification) fan out one repository call per selected type and merge+dedupe+re-sort the results with a new
32	`EntryMerger.mergeMany()` — the same dedupe-by-ID idea RF07's `EntryMerger.merge()` already implements,
33	extended to N equal-weight sources instead of a primary/secondary pair. The one genuinely new domain concept
34	this unit introduces is `DateRangeOption` (a pure, testable date-range → `dateFrom`/`dateTo` mapping) and
35	`ActiveFilterChip` (a pure derivation of which removable chips the screen shows) — both total functions with
36	zero I/O, directly unit-testable like every other `records/domain/` helper RF07 already shipped.
37	
38	## Technical Context
39	
40	**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
41	F000/RF01/RF02/RF03/RF07.
42	
43	**Primary Dependencies**: No additions. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
44	`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`), `go_router`; dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`. The 300 ms debounce is
45	implemented with a plain `dart:async` `Timer` inside `RecordsBloc` (the same primitive
46	`login_signup_page.dart` already uses for its own 300 ms RNF01 loading-indicator delay) — research.md R4
47	explicitly rejects adding `rxdart`/`bloc_concurrency` for this, since a single `Timer` + a monotonic
48	generation counter already gives both the debounce and the request-supersession guarantee FR-002/FR-005a need.
49	
50	**Storage**: No new persistence. "Offline shows cached results" (FR-010/User Story 4) falls out of the
51	existing pattern RF07's `_fetchNextPage` failure branch already established — a failed fetch never clears
52	`RecordsLoaded.entries` — extended here to every new fetch path this unit adds (research.md R7). No local
53	database, no new secure-storage key, no new in-memory store beyond the `RecordsLoaded` fields already planned.
54	
55	**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via
56	`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now exercising
