(`specs/005-multi-source-timeline/`), already implemented — this is the unit that makes RF07's own inert
search bar and funnel button on "Meus Registros" actually do something.

## Summary

"Meus Registros" gains a live semantic search bar (`GET /entries/search`'s `q`, 300 ms debounced) and a filter
sheet (date-range + entry-type, mapped to `GET /entries`'/`GET /entries/search`'s shared `dateFrom`/`dateTo`/
`source` parameters), both narrowing the same `RecordsLoaded` list RF07 already renders. No new screen, no new
bloc: the already-built `RecordsBloc` is extended in place with six new events (`SearchTextChanged`,
`FilterSheetApplied`, `FilterChipRemoved`, `FiltersAndSearchCleared`, `CriteriaLoadRetried`, and an internal
`SearchDebounceElapsed`) and five new `RecordsLoaded` fields (the currently-applied
`searchQuery`/`dateRange`/`entryTypes`, plus `isApplyingCriteria`/`criteriaLoadFailure`), because
the two things RF06 must guarantee — "a new action supersedes any in-flight earlier one" (FR-005a) and "AND
across axes, OR within the entry-type axis" (FR-005) — both need a single, already-serialized owner of
"what the current criteria is and which fetch is the latest one," which is exactly what one bloc already is.
`EntriesRepository.list()` gains optional `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`limit` parameters (additive, RF07's own
cursor-pagination callers unaffected) and gains a new `search()` method (`GET /entries/search`, bounded,
no cursor — FR-005b). Multi-select entry types (`source` is single-valued; FR-003/FR-005's resolved
Clarification) fan out one repository call per selected type and merge+dedupe+re-sort the results with a new
`EntryMerger.mergeMany()` — the same dedupe-by-ID idea RF07's `EntryMerger.merge()` already implements,
extended to N equal-weight sources instead of a primary/secondary pair. The one genuinely new domain concept
this unit introduces is `DateRangeOption` (a pure, testable date-range → `dateFrom`/`dateTo` mapping) and
`ActiveFilterChip` (a pure derivation of which removable chips the screen shows) — both total functions with
zero I/O, directly unit-testable like every other `records/domain/` helper RF07 already shipped.

implemented with a plain `dart:async` `Timer` inside `RecordsBloc` (the same primitive
`login_signup_page.dart` already uses for its own 300 ms RNF01 loading-indicator delay) — research.md R4
explicitly rejects adding `rxdart`/`bloc_concurrency` for this, since a single `Timer` + a monotonic
generation counter already gives both the debounce and the request-supersession guarantee FR-002/FR-005a need.

database, no new secure-storage key, no new in-memory store beyond the `RecordsLoaded` fields already planned.

42	- `thisMonth` → `from` = the 1st of the current local calendar month at local 00:00:00, `to` = `null`.
43

45	(matching the `date-time` format every other date field in `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already
46	uses, and the same `DateTime.parse`/`.toLocal()` round-trip `entries_remote_data_source.dart`/`record_card.dart`
47	already establish for `occurredAt`).

50	defining their exact boundaries — this is squarely "where these documents are silent." Leaving `dateTo` open
51	(`null`, meaning "through now") is simpler and avoids an off-by-one risk at the exact current instant; nothing
52	created in the future exists to accidentally include. The function takes `now` as a parameter
53	(`boundsAt(DateTime now)`), mirroring RF07's `DateGrouper.group(..., {DateTime? now})` precedent, purely so
54	tests can fix "today" deterministically.

57	because a calendar-week boundary reads more naturally against the prototype's Portuguese label ("Esta semana")
58	and matches how `DateGrouper` already buckets by calendar day, not by a rolling window.

68	already defined by RF07)**... ordered by relevance" — explicitly the same entity, not a new one. The only
69	thing `GET /entries/search`'s response adds over `GET /entries`'s is one extra, optional field
70	(`similarity`, 0–1), needed solely to re-sort a multi-type merge by relevance (R1). Every other field in the
71	`entries-search` response schema is identical to `entries-list`/`entries-create`'s. Modeling it as a sibling
72	optional field keeps `record_card.dart` and every other `Entry` consumer unchanged (nothing reads
73	`similarity` outside `EntryMerger.mergeMany()`'s relevance-sort branch) and keeps `EntryMerger.mergeMany()`
74	able to merge `list()`'s and `search()`'s results through one shared type, which per-type fan-out (R1) needs
75	when some types are fetched via `list()` and others — never, actually, since a given fetch round is either

89	can pass `Duration.zero`.

105

107	`showModalBottomSheet` future resolves, re-merging `EntriesRepository.cachedEntries` — RF07's own mechanism)

110	
111	**Rationale**: `cachedEntries` holds every locally-created entry regardless of its `source`/`occurredAt` —
112	RF07 could merge it in unconditionally because nothing on that screen ever filtered. Under an active search
113	term or filter, a just-created entry might not satisfy the current criteria (wrong `source`, outside the

126	
127	**Decision**: a single private `int _fetchGeneration = 0` field on `RecordsBloc`. Every fetch-initiating

133	once it resolves.

141	lever available, and it is sufficient: a discarded response simply never reaches `emit`.

149	
150	**Decision**: no `ConnectivityChecker` pre-check is added before `search()`/`list()` calls, and no new "is

169	handle the resulting `Either`. Introducing the check only for RF06's reads would be an inconsistency with
170	RF07's already-shipped, unmodified pattern for no stated benefit.

(a real offline device), so the offline case reaches the exact same failure-preserving branch every other
network failure does — no special-casing needed. "Reconciles without duplicating any entry" (FR-010's second
half) is `EntryMerger`'s existing dedupe-by-ID behavior (`merge`/`mergeMany`), already guaranteed for any
successful refetch regardless of what triggered it.

**Alternatives considered**: proactively checking `ConnectivityChecker.hasConnection()` before firing a
search/filter request (as `capture/`'s write-path use cases do) — rejected: those checks exist because a
*write* must never be attempted offline (RNF03/capture's own FR); a *read* has no such constraint, and RF07's
own `list()`/`getById()` never pre-check connectivity either — they let the HTTP client fail naturally and
handle the resulting `Either`. Introducing the check only for RF06's reads would be an inconsistency with
RF07's already-shipped, unmodified pattern for no stated benefit.

# Cerne backend — documentation package

The backend is already built and frozen. This package documents what the app needs to consume it. The backend source code is not part of it.

## Contents

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `api/openapi.yaml` | API contract of the 23 endpoints — the source of truth |
| `error-taxonomy.md` | The 13 error codes, with HTTP status and `retryable` |
| `export-screen-states.md` | Mapping between the export screen states and the export job statuses (RF05) |
| `sync-badge.md` | Semantics of the per-entry synchronization badge |
| `known-bugs.md` | Known non-blocking backend defects, with workarounds |
| `fixtures/` | Test media (audio, images for OCR), the expected transcription of the audio, and the three seeded entries used by semantic search |

Credentials (project URL and keys) are not in this package: they are provided in the app's `.env`.

## Contract path → function

`api/openapi.yaml` has no router: each operation is served by its own Edge Function at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` (see `servers` and each operation's `x-cerne-function` in the YAML) — **never** directly at the REST path below. Path parameters are appended as the final URL segments, in the same order as they appear in the path; any literal segment after the last parameter (e.g., the `/retry` of `chat.messages.retry`) does not exist in the real URL.

| Contract path | Function (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>`) |
|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | `auth-signup` |
| `POST /auth/login` | `auth-login` |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | `auth-refresh` |
| `GET /auth/session` | `auth-session` |
| `POST /auth/logout` | `auth-logout` |
| `POST /entries` | `entries-create` |
| `GET /entries` | `entries-list` |
| `GET /entries/{id}` | `entries-get` |
| `GET /entries/search` | `entries-search` |
| `POST /media/ocr` | `media-ocr` |
| `POST /chat/sessions` | `chat-sessions-create` |
| `GET /chat/sessions` | `chat-sessions-list` |
| `GET /chat/sessions/{id}/messages` | `chat-messages-list` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages` | `chat-messages-send` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages/{userMessageId}/retry` | `chat-messages-retry` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/insight` | `chat-insight-create` |
| `POST /export/summary` | `export-summary-create` |
| `GET /export/{jobId}/status` | `export-status-get` |
| `GET /export/{jobId}/download` | `export-download-get` |
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate` | `dashboard-aggregate-get` |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative` | `dashboard-narrative-get` |
| `PATCH /account/settings` | `account-settings-update` |
| `DELETE /account` | `account-delete` |

# Known bugs

Non-blocking backend defects found after the backend was frozen, each with a workaround.

| Date | Endpoint / area | Description | Workaround | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| _(empty — no defect recorded so far)_ | | | | |
---ERRORTAX---
# Error taxonomy — 13 codes

Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.

| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |

**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.

**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.
---FIXTURES---

46	## 2. Navigable states
47	
48	Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.
49	
50	### 2.1 Entry and authentication
51	| State | What it shows |
52	|---|---|
53	| Tela 0 — Splash | Wordmark "Cerne" centered on dark green, 3 loading dots; lasts 1.8 s and moves on automatically. |
54	| Tela 0.1 — Biometria | Fingerprint circle, title "Toque para desbloquear", link "Usar PIN", secondary link "usar e-mail e senha" near the bottom. |
55	| Tela 0.1a — Entrar | Login mode: title "Bem-vindo de volta", fields E-mail and Senha, CTA "Entrar", toggle link, link "usar biometria". |
56	| Tela 0.1a — Criar conta | Same screen in sign-up mode: title "Crie sua conta", CTA "Criar conta" (toggled by a text link, not a separate screen). |
57	| Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial | Title "Digite seu PIN", 4 progress dots, 3×4 numeric keypad with backspace; after the 4th digit, moves on after 350 ms. |
58	| Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha | Same as 0.1b plus the error band "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN". |
59	
60	### 2.2 Conversation
61	| State | What it shows |
62	|---|---|
63	| Tela 1 — Home/Chat (default) | Messages going back and forth; dark green fixed header with ☰ and wordmark; composer with "+", placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...", send icon. |
64	| Tela 1 — Streaming | AI response revealed progressively with a pulsing cursor. |
65	| Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label "INSIGHT", "x" to dismiss, interleaved in the messages. |
66	| Tela 1 — Falha ao gerar resposta | Incomplete AI message with "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" in red, in place of the time. |
67	| Tela 1 — Bookmark | Bookmark on each user message with 4 sub-states: `idle`, `saving` (spinner), `saved` (ochre check), `error` (red warning). |
68	| Tela 1 — Offline | Blue-gray banner "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas"; send icon disabled. |
69	| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
70	| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |
71	
72	### 2.3 Insertion modal (bottom sheet over Home/Chat; 9 states)
73	Common structure: "x" to close and a 3-tab bar (Texto / Áudio / Foto); the active tab has a filled dark-green background.
74	
75	| State | What it shows |
76	|---|---|
77	| Texto | Multiline field, placeholder "Escreva livremente...", button "Salvar". |
78	| Áudio — Gravando | Red stop button, animated 12-bar waveform, monospace timer (e.g., "00:12"). |
79	| Áudio — Processando | Spinner in place of stop; frozen, faded waveform (opacity .35); text "Transcrevendo..."; label "00:42 de áudio". |
80	| Áudio — Transcrito | Editable transcribed text; original audio duration in mono; "Salvar" enabled. |
81	| Áudio — Erro | Red warning icon, "Não foi possível transcrever", outline button "Tentar novamente". |
82	| Foto — Captura | Two large buttons, "Câmera" and "Galeria". |
83	| Foto — Processando OCR | Photo thumbnail, spinner, "Reconhecendo texto...". |
84	| Foto — Reconhecido | Small thumbnail next to the extracted (editable) text; "Salvar". |
85	| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |
86	
87	### 2.4 Records
88	| State | What it shows |
89	|---|---|
90	| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
91	| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |
92	| Tela 4 — Filtros ativos | Removable chips under the search bar with the applied filters, link "Limpar filtros"; funnel button filled. |
93	| Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro | Groups "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, single choice), "CATEGORIA" (chips: trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (chips: manual, áudio, foto, chat); "Aplicar" and "Limpar". **Note:** the backend has no category filter (requirements, RF06); categories are the tags extension. |
94	
95	### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
96	| State | What it shows |
97	|---|---|
98	| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
99	| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
100	| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |
101	| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
102	| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |
103	
104	All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.
105	
106	### 2.6 Plans and settings
107	| State | What it shows |
108	|---|---|
109	| Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]** | Three horizontally scrolling columns — "A Fazer", "Em Andamento", "Concluído" — with counts and cards. |
110	| Tela 6 — Configurações — mais de 30 registros | "Sua evolução": 10-bar ochre chart + summary paragraph. |
111	| Tela 6 — Configurações — uma entrada | A single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias." |
112	| Tela 6 — Configurações — zero entradas | Light-gray chart icon in place of the chart and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; no summary paragraph. |
113	| Tela 6 — Configurações — narrativa indisponível | Chart with data, but the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own error message, not just missing text. |
114	| Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta | Centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?", text on permanent, irreversible deletion; red button "Apagar tudo"; outline "Cancelar". |
115	
116	Other elements of Configurações: avatar with editable name/e-mail (pencil becomes a check in edit mode — inline editing); persona cards "Como a IA responde" (Analítico, Empático, Socrático) **[ext]**; actions "Sair" and "Apagar conta" (red).
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 3. Visual system (tokens for `design_tokens.dart`)
121	
122	The prototype has a **Design Tokens** panel, marked as the ground truth for `design_tokens.dart`. Its names and values are below.
123	
124	### Colors
125	| Token | Hex | Use (as stated in the panel) |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| `colorPrimary` | `#1F3D34` | Buttons, app bar, wordmark |
128	| `colorPrimaryPressed` | `#16281F` | Pressed state |
129	| `colorOnPrimary` | `#F5F1E8` | Text on primary |
130	| `colorAccent` | `#C98A3E` | CTA, insight, saved bookmark |
131	| `colorOnAccent` | `#241C0D` | Text on accent |
132	| `colorSecondary` | `#7C8B6F` | Tags, chips, synchronizing |
133	| `colorSurfaceBg` | `#F2EFE7` | General background ("paper") |
134	| `colorSurfaceElevated` | `#FBF9F4` | Cards, bubbles, sheets |
135	| `colorBorder` | `#E1DACB` | Dividers, borders |
136	| `colorTextPrimary` | `#241F19` | Main text |
137	| `colorTextSecondary` | `#6B6255` | Secondary text |
138	| `colorError` | `#B3402A` | Errors, destructive action |
139	| `colorSuccess` | `#4C6B4F` | Synchronized, confirmations |
140	| `colorWarningSync` | `#C98A3E` | "Synchronizing" badge |
141	| `colorInfoOffline` | `#5C7A93` | Offline banner — single use |
142	
143	Other colors that appear on specific screens but not in the panel: user chat bubble `#D9DFD3`; text on category chips `#3F4A38`.

1	# Data Model: P-RF06 — Semantic search / filter
2	
3	Source: spec.md §Key Entities, requirements.md §§1 (RF06), 6.2, 6.4, 8, 10, 13; `docs/input/backend/api/
4	openapi.yaml`'s `/entries` and `/entries/search` schemas; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.4.
5	This unit extends `entries/`'s shared `Entry`/`EntriesRepository` (RF01/RF07) and `records/`'s `RecordsBloc`/
6	`EntryMerger` (RF07) — it introduces two small new pure domain entities (`DateRangeOption`,
7	`ActiveFilterChip`) and widens two already-existing shapes (`Entry`, `EntryMerger`).
8	
9	## `Entry` (`lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart`) — extended, not replaced
10	
11	One new field, nullable, additive (research.md R3):
12	
13	```dart
14	class Entry extends Equatable {
15	  const Entry({
16	    required this.id,
17	    // ...all existing fields, unchanged...
18	    this.similarity,   // NEW — 0.0–1.0, only ever non-null when parsed from `entries-search`'s response
19	  });
20	
21	  final double? similarity;
22	
23	  @override
24	  List<Object?> get props => [/* ...existing fields..., */ similarity];
25	}
26	```
27	
28	Every existing construction site (RF01's `create()`, RF07's `list()`/`getById()`) omits it, so it defaults to
29	`null` — no behavior change for any existing consumer (`record_card.dart`, `DateGrouper`, `EntryMerger.merge`).
30	
31	## `EntriesRepository` — extended (`lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`)
32	
33	```dart
34	abstract class EntriesRepository {
35	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({required String content, required EntrySource source});  // unchanged
36	
37	  List<Entry> get cachedEntries;                                                                    // unchanged
38	
39	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({
40	    String? cursor,
41	    EntrySource? source,     // NEW — GET /entries's existing `source` parameter
42	    DateTime? dateFrom,      // NEW — GET /entries's existing `dateFrom` parameter
43	    DateTime? dateTo,        // NEW — GET /entries's existing `dateTo` parameter
44	    int? limit,              // NEW — GET /entries's existing `limit` parameter; omitted ⇒ backend default (20)
45	  });
46	
47	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);                                                // unchanged
48	
49	  /// `GET /entries/search` (`entries-search`) — bounded, no cursor (FR-005b). Retries exactly once through
50	  /// `SessionRepository.refresh()` on `AuthExpiredFailure`, same as `list()`/`getById()` (research.md R6 of
51	  /// RF07's own plan, reused verbatim here).
52	  Future<Either<Failure, List<Entry>>> search({
53	    String? q,
54	    EntrySource? source,
55	    DateTime? dateFrom,
56	    DateTime? dateTo,
57	    int limit = 50,          // the endpoint's own maximum (openapi.yaml) — see research.md R1
58	  });
59	}
60	```
61	
62	- `list()`'s four new parameters are each omitted from the request's `queryParameters` map when `null` —
63	  every existing call site (`RecordsBloc._loadFirstPage`/`_fetchNextPage` before this unit) is byte-for-byte
64	  unaffected.
65	- `search()` has no `cursor` parameter at all — `GET /entries/search` doesn't accept one (openapi.yaml).
66	
67	### `EntriesRemoteDataSource` — extended (`lib/features/entries/data/entries_remote_data_source.dart`)
68	
69	- `list()` passes `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`limit` through to `ApiClient.call(..., queryParameters: {...})`
70	  exactly like RF07's `cursor` already does (string-keyed map, `null` entries omitted); `dateFrom`/`dateTo` are
71	  sent as `.toUtc().toIso8601String()`.
72	- `search()` calls `ApiClient.call('entries-search', method: 'GET', queryParameters: {...}, unwrapData:
73	  false)` — same `unwrapData: false` shape `list()` already uses, since the response is `{"data": [...],
74	  "meta": {"mode": ...}}`; `meta.mode` (`filter_only`/`semantic`) is read by the backend only, never consumed
75	  by the app (research.md — spec.md's own Clarification 2 already names which endpoint handles which case, so
76	  nothing here needs to branch on `meta.mode`).
77	- Both `list()`'s and `search()`'s per-entry parsing go through the *same* `_parseEntryFields` helper RF07
78	  already extracted, now additionally reading `data['similarity'] as num?` → `.toDouble()` when present (it
79	  never is for `entries-list`/`entries-get`/`entries-create` responses, so existing call sites keep getting
80	  `similarity: null`).
81	
82	### `EntriesRepositoryImpl` — extended (`lib/features/entries/data/entries_repository_impl.dart`)
83	
84	`search()` is implemented with the exact same `_retryAfterSilentRefresh` helper `list()`/`getById()` already
85	use — no new retry logic. No new constructor dependency (still just `EntriesRemoteDataSource` +
86	`SessionRepository`, unchanged from RF07).
87	
88	## `DateRangeOption` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/date_range_filter.dart`) — NEW
89	
90	```dart
91	enum DateRangeOption { allTime, thisWeek, thisMonth }
92	
93	extension DateRangeBounds on DateRangeOption {
94	  /// Pure, total; `now` defaults to `DateTime.now()` but is overridable for deterministic tests
95	  /// (research.md R2, mirroring `DateGrouper.group(..., {DateTime? now})`'s existing precedent).
96	  ({DateTime? from, DateTime? to}) boundsAt(DateTime now) => switch (this) {
97	    DateRangeOption.allTime => (from: null, to: null),
98	    DateRangeOption.thisWeek => (from: _mostRecentMonday(now), to: null),
99	    DateRangeOption.thisMonth => (from: DateTime(now.year, now.month), to: null),
100	  };
101	}
102	```
103	
104	No `package:flutter` import, no I/O — pure `DateTime` arithmetic (research.md R2).
105	
106	**Prototype label mapping** (prototype-extract.md §2.4's "Sheet de filtro", "INTERVALO DE DATA" group, single
107	choice):
108	
109	| `DateRangeOption` | Label |
110	|---|---|
111	| `allTime` | "Todo o período" |
112	| `thisWeek` | "Esta semana" |
113	| `thisMonth` | "Este mês" |
114	
115	## `ActiveFilterChip` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/active_filter_chip.dart`) — NEW
116	
117	```dart
118	sealed class ActiveFilterChip extends Equatable {
119	  const ActiveFilterChip();
120	}
121	
122	class DateRangeChip extends ActiveFilterChip {
123	  const DateRangeChip(this.option);          // option is never DateRangeOption.allTime (see derive() below)
124	  final DateRangeOption option;
125	  @override List<Object?> get props => [option];
126	}
127	
128	class EntryTypeChip extends ActiveFilterChip {
129	  const EntryTypeChip(this.source);
130	  final EntrySource source;
131	  @override List<Object?> get props => [source];
132	}
133	
134	class ActiveFilterChips {
135	  const ActiveFilterChips._();
136	
137	  /// Pure derivation — one chip per currently-applied Filter Set criterion (Key Entities: "Active Filter
138	  /// Chip"). The active search term is deliberately NOT a chip here (FR-006 scopes chips to the Filter Set —
139	  /// date range + entry types — not the Search Query, a separate Key Entity); "Limpar filtros" still clears
140	  /// both (FR-007).
141	  static List<ActiveFilterChip> derive({
142	    required DateRangeOption dateRange,
143	    required Set<EntrySource> entryTypes,
144	  }) => [
145	    if (dateRange != DateRangeOption.allTime) DateRangeChip(dateRange),
146	    for (final source in entryTypes) EntryTypeChip(source),
147	  ];
148	}
149	```
150	
151	## `EntryMerger` (`lib/features/records/domain/entities/entry_merger.dart`) — extended
152	
153	```dart
154	class EntryMerger {
155	  const EntryMerger._();
156	
157	  static List<Entry> merge({required List<Entry> primary, required List<Entry> secondary});  // unchanged (RF07)
158	
159	  /// NEW — N equal-weight sources (one per selected entry type, research.md R1), deduped by id (last write
160	  /// wins; in practice no two sources ever share an id, since every entry has exactly one `source`), sorted
161	  /// either by `similarity` (an active search term) or by `occurredAt` (no search term) — FR-005's "re-sorted
162	  /// ... by relevance when a search term is active, otherwise reverse-chronological."
163	  static List<Entry> mergeMany({
164	    required List<List<Entry>> sources,
165	    required bool byRelevance,
166	  }) {
167	    final byId = <String, Entry>{};
168	    for (final list in sources) {
169	      for (final entry in list) {
170	        byId[entry.id] = entry;
171	      }
172	    }
173	    final merged = byId.values.toList();
174	    merged.sort(
175	      byRelevance
176	          ? (a, b) => (b.similarity ?? 0).compareTo(a.similarity ?? 0)
177	          : (a, b) => b.occurredAt.compareTo(a.occurredAt),
178	    );
179	    return merged;
180	  }
181	}
182	```
183	
184	`mergeMany` is used both when 2+ entry types are selected (R1) and, trivially, with a single-element `sources`
185	list for the ordinary single-type-or-no-type search path — keeping exactly one merge/sort code path for every
186	bounded fetch, rather than a special case for "only one type selected."
187	
188	## `RecordsEvent` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_event.dart`) — extended
189	
190	| Event | When |
191	|---|---|
192	| `RecordsStarted` | Unchanged (RF07). |
193	| `NextPageRequested` | Unchanged (RF07) — now a no-op whenever the current criteria is bounded (R1/FR-005b), because `nextCursor` is `null` in that case. |
194	| `PageLoadRetried` | Unchanged (RF07) for a first-load/next-page failure; see `CriteriaLoadRetried` below for a criteria-change failure. |
195	| `RecordsLocalCacheRefreshed` | Unchanged signature; behavior gains the "no-op while criteria active" guard (research.md R5). |
196	| `SearchTextChanged(String text)` | **NEW** — the search bar's `onChanged`, fired on every keystroke. |
197	| `SearchDebounceElapsed(String text)` *(internal)* | **NEW** — fired by the bloc's own `Timer`, 300 ms after the last `SearchTextChanged` with non-empty text; never dispatched directly by any widget. |
198	| `FilterSheetApplied({required DateRangeOption dateRange, required Set<EntrySource> entryTypes})` | **NEW** — the filter sheet's "Aplicar" button. |
199	| `FilterChipRemoved(ActiveFilterChip chip)` | **NEW** — tapping a single active-filter chip's remove control. |
200	| `FiltersAndSearchCleared` | **NEW** — "Limpar filtros" (clears date range, entry types, **and** the search text — FR-007). |
201	| `CriteriaLoadRetried` | **NEW** — "Tentar novamente" on a failed criteria-change fetch (`criteriaLoadFailure`); re-attempts the same last-applied criteria. |
202	
203	## `RecordsState` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_state.dart`) — extended
204	
205	```dart
206	class RecordsLoaded extends RecordsState {
207	  const RecordsLoaded({
208	    required this.entries,
209	    required this.nextCursor,          // null whenever the current criteria is bounded (R1) — see hasReachedEnd
210	    required this.isLoadingMore,
211	    this.pageLoadFailure,              // unchanged (RF07) — a further-page (unbounded-mode) fetch failed
212	    this.searchQuery = '',             // NEW
213	    this.dateRange = DateRangeOption.allTime,   // NEW
214	    this.entryTypes = const {},        // NEW
215	    this.isApplyingCriteria = false,   // NEW — a criteria-change fetch is in flight (RNF01's >300ms affordance)
216	    this.criteriaLoadFailure,          // NEW — a criteria-change fetch failed; entries/criteria fields unchanged
217	  });
218	
219	  final List<Entry> entries;
220	  final String? nextCursor;
221	  final bool isLoadingMore;
222	  final Failure? pageLoadFailure;
223	  final String searchQuery;
224	  final DateRangeOption dateRange;
225	  final Set<EntrySource> entryTypes;
226	  final bool isApplyingCriteria;
227	  final Failure? criteriaLoadFailure;
228	
229	  bool get hasReachedEnd => nextCursor == null;
230	  bool get isEmpty => entries.isEmpty;
231	
232	  bool get isSearchActive => searchQuery.isNotEmpty;
233	  bool get hasActiveFilters => dateRange != DateRangeOption.allTime || entryTypes.isNotEmpty;
234	  bool get hasAnyActiveCriteria => isSearchActive || hasActiveFilters;
235	
236	  List<ActiveFilterChip> get activeChips =>
237	      ActiveFilterChips.derive(dateRange: dateRange, entryTypes: entryTypes);
238	
239	  /// FR-009 — distinct from `isEmpty` alone: only true when narrowing (not a true zero-entries account)
240	  /// produced the empty result.
241	  bool get isEmptyForCriteria => isEmpty && hasAnyActiveCriteria;
242	}
243	```
244	
245	- `RecordsLoading`/`RecordsLoadFailure` are unchanged from RF07 — still only used for the very first app-level
246	  load, before any `RecordsLoaded` exists to carry criteria.
247	- `isEmptyForCriteria` vs. plain `isEmpty` is what `RecordsPage` uses to choose between
248	  `no_results_for_criteria_view.dart` (FR-009) and RF07's unmodified `records_empty_state.dart`
249	  (account-wide "Nenhum registro ainda").
250	
251	## `RecordsBloc` (`lib/features/records/presentation/bloc/records_bloc.dart`) — extended
252	
253	```dart
254	class RecordsBloc extends Bloc<RecordsEvent, RecordsState> {
255	  RecordsBloc({
256	    required EntriesRepository entriesRepository,
257	    Duration debounceDuration = const Duration(milliseconds: 300),   // NEW, injectable (research.md R4)
258	  });
259	
260	  Stream<void> get reauthRequired;   // unchanged (RF07)
261	}
262	```
263	
264	New private state: `String _query = ''`, `DateRangeOption _dateRange = DateRangeOption.allTime`,
265	`Set<EntrySource> _entryTypes = {}`, `Timer? _debounceTimer`, `int _fetchGeneration = 0` — see
266	`contracts/records-bloc-extension.md` for the exact handler-by-handler sequencing (debounce, generation
267	guard, bounded-vs-paginated branch, and how `FilterChipRemoved`/`FiltersAndSearchCleared` each re-fetch).
268	
269	Still depends only on `EntriesRepository` — no new constructor dependency (research.md's Post-Design
270	Constitution Check).
271	
272	## Widgets (`lib/features/records/presentation/`) — new/changed
273	
274	Not separately contracted beyond `contracts/filter-sheet-widget.md` (pure prototype-fidelity rendering, no new
275	domain logic beyond what's above):
276	
277	- `records_page.dart` — `_SearchBar`'s `TextField` becomes `enabled: true`, dispatching `SearchTextChanged` on
278	  every change; the funnel button's `onPressed` opens `FilterSheet` via `showModalBottomSheet`, and its icon
279	  swaps to the filled variant whenever `RecordsLoaded.hasActiveFilters` is true (FR-006). `_buildLoaded` adds
280	  the `ActiveFilterChipsRow` (only when `activeChips.isNotEmpty`) directly under `_SearchBar`, and branches
281	  `isEmptyForCriteria` to `NoResultsForCriteriaView` instead of `RecordsEmptyState`.
282	- `filter_sheet.dart` — **NEW**. A `StatefulWidget` holding its own local, uncommitted selections
283	  (`_localDateRange`, `_localEntryTypes`, `_localCategoryChips` — the last never leaves this widget, FR-004).
284	  "Aplicar" dispatches `FilterSheetApplied` with the local selections and closes the sheet; "Limpar" resets
285	  only this widget's own local `State` (no dispatch, no close — Story 2/Acceptance Scenario 3).
286	- `active_filter_chips_row.dart` — **NEW**. One removable chip per `RecordsLoaded.activeChips` entry (label
287	  via `DateRangeOption`'s mapping table above or `EntrySource`'s existing name), each dispatching
288	  `FilterChipRemoved(chip)`; a trailing "Limpar filtros" `TextButton` dispatching `FiltersAndSearchCleared`.
289	- `no_results_for_criteria_view.dart` — **NEW**. Distinct copy from `records_empty_state.dart` (FR-009), with
290	  a button that dispatches `FiltersAndSearchCleared` ("adjust or clear the applied criteria").
291	
292	**Token reuse** (prototype-extract.md §2.4 — no new token, Principle IV):
293	
294	| Element | Token |
295	|---|---|
296	| Filter sheet surface | `DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated` |
297	| Filter sheet group labels ("INTERVALO DE DATA" etc.) | `DesignTokens.textLabelMd` + `colorTextSecondary` |
298	| Unselected chip | `DesignTokens.colorSurfaceBg` fill, `colorBorder` side (same as `record_card.dart`'s tag chips) |
299	| Selected chip (date-range radio or entry-type multi-select) | `DesignTokens.colorPrimary` fill, `colorOnPrimary` text |
300	| Active-filter chip / filled funnel button | `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (matches the prototype's funnel-filled state) |
301	| "Limpar filtros" link | `DesignTokens.textLabelMd` + `colorAccent` |
302

# Research: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

Phase 0 output. Each item is a reasonable technical decision made under Constitution Principle I ("where these
documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on
clarification"). None reopens one of spec.md's own three already-resolved Clarifications (title derivation,
side-menu ordering/pagination, offline cache scope) — each item below fills in a mechanical detail those
Clarifications, the OpenAPI contract, or the prototype extract leave open.

## R1 — How is the SSE response (`chat-messages-send`/`chat-messages-retry`) consumed without a new dependency?

**Decision**: `ApiClient` (core/network) gains one new method, `sseStream(...)`, built on `dio`'s own
`ResponseType.stream` — the same `Dio` instance every other call already goes through, just configured to
return a raw byte stream (`ResponseBody.stream`) instead of buffering/decoding a JSON body. It:
1. Issues the request with `Options(method: 'POST', responseType: ResponseType.stream, headers: {...})` —
   same `apikey`/`Authorization` headers every other call already sends.
2. Decodes the byte stream as UTF-8 and buffers it into lines, splitting on the blank-line (`\n\n`) SSE frame
   delimiter — a frame is one or more `field: value` lines; this unit only ever needs `event:` and `data:`.
3. Yields `Right(SseFrame(event: ..., data: ...))` for each parsed frame, in arrival order.
4. Catches `DioException` the same way `call()`'s own `_mapException` already does (timeout → retryable
   `NetworkTimeoutFailure`; no response at all → `NetworkOfflineFailure`; a response body that *is* JSON and
   carries `{code, message, retryable}` → `ErrorMapper.fromResponse`), yielding exactly one `Left(failure)` as
   the stream's last item, then closes the stream normally (never a Dart-level `Stream.error`/exception).

**Rationale**: `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s own schema for both SSE operations is `content:
text/event-stream` / `schema: {type: string}` — i.e., "a stream of bytes," with no generated Dart client
possible for it the way `call()`'s JSON responses already have. Every other HTTP primitive this app needs
(headers, auth mode, the exact mapped `Failure` taxonomy) already lives in `ApiClient`; duplicating that logic
in a second, chat-specific HTTP client would violate Principle II's "single, non-negotiable stack" spirit for
no benefit. A hand-rolled SSE line-parser is ~30 lines over a byte stream `dio` already exposes — simpler than
adding a transitive dependency (e.g., `flutter_client_sse`, which also assumes `http`/its own client stack,
not `dio`) for a 5-field-type protocol this app will only ever speak to one backend.

**Alternatives considered**: a third-party SSE package — rejected, new dependency, and every such package
assumes it owns the HTTP call itself, which would mean either a second client stack alongside `dio` or
fighting the package's API to reuse `ApiClient`'s existing auth/header logic; `package:http`'s
`Client.send()` + manual stream handling — rejected for the same "two HTTP stacks" reason, since `dio` can do
the identical byte-stream thing `ApiClient` already needs.

## R2 — What does each SSE event's `data` payload contain?

**Decision**: the five event types the sequence names (`message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`)
carry JSON payloads inferred as follows, each parsed by `ChatRemoteDataSource` (never by the generic
`ApiClient.sseStream`, which only hands back `{event, data}` string pairs):

| Event | Assumed `data` shape | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `message_created` | `{"userMessageId": "<uuid>", "assistantMessageId": "<uuid>"}` | Reconciling the two optimistic local placeholders (R5) with their real backend ids — `userMessageId` is also the exact value later needed as `POST .../retry`'s path parameter. |
| `context` | opaque/ignorable (spec.md's own Assumptions: "an internal signal the client may use to drive its own progress indicator, not a citation list") | Nothing beyond confirming the stream is progressing — no field is read. |
| `token` | `{"delta": "<string>"}` | Appended to the assistant placeholder's `content`, in arrival order. |
| `done` | `{"assistantMessageId": "<uuid>", "content": "<full final text>", "createdAt": "<ISO-8601>"}` | Finalizing the assistant message: status → `complete`, content replaced with the server's own authoritative final text (not just the locally-concatenated tokens, in case of any drift), timestamp set. |
| `error` (backend-named SSE event, business-level failure — distinct from a transport-level `DioException`) | the same `{code, message, retryable}` envelope every other endpoint's error body already uses | Mapped through the *same* `ErrorMapper.fromResponse` every other failure path uses, so `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`/`RATE_LIMITED`/etc. all resolve to the one shared `Failure` taxonomy. |

**Rationale**: the OpenAPI schema is silent on field names (`schema: {type: string}` for the whole stream),
so this is squarely "where these documents are silent." The chosen field names follow this codebase's own
established conventions verbatim — every REST response already uses `userMessageId`/`assistantMessageId`-style
camelCase ids (e.g., `entries`'s `chatMessageId`), every error already uses `{code, message, retryable}`
(`error-taxonomy.md`), and `createdAt` is the exact field name `chat-messages-list`'s own response schema uses
for a message's timestamp. Re-using the identical error envelope for the backend-named `error` SSE event means
`ChatRemoteDataSource` needs exactly one error-parsing code path (`ErrorMapper.fromResponse`) for every
failure source in this unit — transport-level, business-level, and every other endpoint already built.

**Alternatives considered**: guessing a flatter shape (e.g., `token`'s data being the raw delta string, not
JSON) — rejected because every other endpoint in this contract wraps its payload in JSON, and an un-keyed raw
string would be the only exception; treating `done`'s `content` as redundant with the locally-concatenated
tokens and skipping it — rejected, since trusting the server's own final text over a client-side concatenation
guards against any dropped/reordered-token edge case with no added cost.

## R3 — Mid-stream `AUTH_EXPIRED` handling

**Decision**: `ChatRepository.sendMessage()`/`.retryMessage()` retries the *entire call* exactly once via
`SessionRepository.refresh()` — mirroring `EntriesRepositoryImpl._retryAfterSilentRefresh` — **only** when the
very first item the stream produces is `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` (i.e., the stream failed before any
`ChatStreamEvent` was ever successfully emitted). If `AuthExpiredFailure` arrives after at least one
`ChatStreamEvent` has already been emitted (the turn is already visibly in progress), it is treated like any
other failure: `ChatBloc` marks that message's status as `failed` (the ordinary "Falha ao gerar resposta" path,
retryable by the user via the existing retry button) *and* separately fires `reauthRequired`, so the
app-wide "Sessão expirada" overlay still appears over the chat — it just does not auto-retry the
already-partially-generated response, which would otherwise risk silently regenerating/duplicating a response
the user never asked to retry.

**Rationale**: the "retry once if the very first attempt is `AuthExpiredFailure`" shape is this codebase's own
existing pattern for every other repository method; extending it unconditionally into "re-run a whole
streaming generation transparently after the user has already seen several tokens" is a materially different,
riskier behavior the spec never describes (FR-006 scopes retry explicitly to the "Falha ao gerar resposta"
tap, a user-initiated action). Keeping the two cases visually distinguishable (transparent retry only
pre-stream vs. surfaced failure + overlay once any token arrived) satisfies FR-005/FR-006 without inventing
mid-stream reconnection logic the OpenAPI contract gives no shape for.

**Alternatives considered**: always surfacing `AUTH_EXPIRED` as a plain failed-message state, never
transparently retrying it even pre-stream — rejected, it would make a session-boundary coincidence (the
access token expiring the instant `chat-messages-send` is called) indistinguishable from a real generation
failure, when every other read path in this app already recovers from that specific case silently.

## R4 — Local cache shape (`ChatLocalCache`)

**Decision**: one new Keychain-backed class, `lib/features/chat/data/chat_local_cache.dart`, mirroring
`EntriesLocalCache`'s pattern (`flutter_secure_storage`, JSON-encoded) but covering three independent pieces of
state, each under its own storage key so one write never clobbers another:
- `chatSessionsLocalCache` → `List<ChatSession>` — every session ever returned by any successful
  `chat-sessions-list` page fetch (merged by id, same `_mergeEntries`-style upsert `EntriesLocalCache` already
  does), satisfying Clarification 3's "the side menu's own session list... remain[s] browsable" while offline.
- `chatMessagesLocalCache` → `Map<String, List<ChatMessage>>` keyed by `sessionId` — written only when that
  specific session's `chat-messages-list` call succeeds, satisfying Clarification 3's "every chat session the
  user has opened at least once while online" (a session never individually fetched never gets a map entry, so
  selecting it offline has nothing to fall back to — the exact "standard no-connection state" Edge Case).
- `chatLastActiveSessionId` → `String?` — which conversation to resume on next app open (spec.md's own
  Assumptions: "Re-opening the app resumes whichever conversation the user was last in"), written every time
  `ChatBloc` successfully switches to or creates a session.

**Rationale**: journal/chat content is exactly the same class of personal data `EntriesLocalCache`'s own
rationale already covers ("personal data, so it stays encrypted at rest like the PIN it already sits behind")
— reusing the identical storage mechanism (not a plain file, not `shared_preferences`, which isn't a project
dependency and isn't encrypted) keeps one consistent at-rest-encryption story for every category of personal
content this app persists locally. Three separate keys (rather than one combined blob) mean a failed/partial
write to one never corrupts or need to recompute the other two, and each is independently simple to merge
(sessions: upsert-by-id like `EntriesLocalCache`; messages: replace-whole-list-for-this-session-id, since
`chat-messages-list` always returns the complete ordered history, never a page).

**Alternatives considered**: a single combined JSON blob (`{sessions: [...], messagesBySession: {...},
lastActiveSessionId: ...}`) under one key — rejected, since it would force rewriting the entire cache (all
sessions' full message histories) on every single page-list fetch, a much larger and slower encrypted write
for no benefit over three independent keys; `sqflite`/a real local database — rejected as a new dependency for
a cache whose total size (a handful of sessions, each a bounded message history) never approaches a scale
that benefits from indexed queries over simple JSON (de)serialization.

## R5 — Optimistic local ids for an in-flight message pair

**Decision**: the moment `MessageSubmitted`/`MessageRetryRequested` fires, `ChatBloc` immediately appends (for
a fresh send) a `ChatMessage(role: user, status: complete, id: 'local-<timestamp>', ...)` and a
`ChatMessage(role: assistant, status: streaming, id: 'local-<timestamp>-response', content: '', ...)` to the
in-memory list — satisfying RNF01's "<100 ms local reflection" before any network round-trip completes. Once
the stream's `message_created` event arrives, both placeholder ids are replaced in place with the real
`userMessageId`/`assistantMessageId` the backend assigned (same list position, same displayed content) — a
pure id swap, invisible to the user. A retry reuses the *existing*, already-real `userMessageId` (it is never
optimistic — retry only ever targets an already-persisted message from a prior turn) and appends only a new
optimistic assistant placeholder for the regenerated response.

**Rationale**: `Entry`/`EntriesRepositoryImpl.create()` already shows this app's established shape for "show
it instantly, reconcile with the server's real id once the call resolves" is not used there (that call isn't
streamed, so the UI simply waits for the single `Either`) — chat is the first flow where a network round-trip
is slow enough, and visibly multi-staged enough (RNF01's instant-local-reflection + the user-visible streaming
state, both before any id exists), that an optimistic placeholder is the only way to satisfy both at once. A
timestamp-prefixed string id needs no new dependency (no `uuid` package) and only ever needs to be
locally-unique for the lifetime of one `ChatBloc` instance, which `DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch` already
guarantees in practice.

**Alternatives considered**: adding the `uuid` package for a "real" UUID-shaped placeholder — rejected, the
id's only two jobs (equality-based list lookup during the swap, and being visibly distinct from every
server-issued id to avoid ever being sent to the backend by mistake) don't need UUID's collision guarantees at
this scale; waiting for `message_created` before showing anything — rejected, directly violates RNF01.

## R6 — Title-derivation algorithm (FR-010)

**Decision**: `ChatTitleDeriver.derive(String firstMessageText)` — a pure function in
`lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_title_deriver.dart` — collapses internal whitespace/newlines to single
spaces, trims, and caps the result at 48 characters, appending `'…'` when truncated. The result is always
non-empty by construction, because the composer already blocks sending empty/whitespace-only text (Edge
Cases) before `ChatBloc` ever calls this function.

**Rationale**: spec.md's own Assumptions explicitly leave "the exact wording of... the derived-title preview
length... a presentation detail left to implementation." 48 characters is chosen to comfortably fit the side
menu's "CONVERSAS" row (prototype-extract.md §2.2: "title + timestamp" on one line) without needing per-device
text-measurement logic — a fixed character cap, not a fixed pixel width, keeps the function pure and testable
(RNF07) with zero `package:flutter` dependency (Principle V). Collapsing whitespace/newlines avoids a
multi-line first message producing a title that visually breaks the single-line list row.

**Alternatives considered**: truncating by word boundary instead of a hard character cut — rejected as
unnecessary complexity for a preview whose only consumer is one list row with its own ellipsis-safe text
widget (`overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis` already handles any remaining visual overflow regardless); no cap at
all (send the full first message as `title`) — rejected, defeats the point of a "preview."

## R7 — Two blocs, no new route; how "Novo Chat" and conversation-switching reach the chat screen

**Decision**: two blocs, both under `lib/features/chat/presentation/bloc/`: `ChatBloc` (the Home/Chat screen's
own conversation — messages, streaming, retry, composer gating, offline banner) and `ChatSessionsBloc` (the
side menu's "CONVERSAS" list — paginated, offline-cached, mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s own shape exactly). Both
are provided once, together, above `HomeChatShellPage`'s `Scaffold` (a `MultiBlocProvider`, replacing today's
bare `const HomeChatShellPage()` route builder in `app_router.dart`) — so `AppDrawer` (rebuilt as a
`StatefulWidget`) and the chat screen's own body share the *same* `ChatBloc` instance for the lifetime of one
visit to `/home`. "Novo Chat" and tapping a past conversation each dispatch directly to that shared `ChatBloc`
(`NewConversationRequested`/`ConversationSelected(sessionId)`) from inside `AppDrawer` — no new `go_router`
route, no `sessionId` path parameter; `AppRoutes.home` stays the single, unparameterized route it already is.
`ChatSessionsBloc` never imports or is imported by `ChatBloc` — `AppDrawer` is the one mediating widget (the
same sanctioned "cross-bloc touch point lives in `presentation/`, never inside a bloc" shape
`records_page.dart` already establishes for `RecordsBloc`/`SessionBloc`), and the drawer's own
`Scaffold.onDrawerChanged` callback dispatches `SessionsRefreshRequested` to `ChatSessionsBloc` every time the
drawer transitions from closed to open — so a session created moments earlier (by sending a first message) is
picked up the next time the user opens the drawer, with no cross-bloc event bus needed.

**Rationale**: `RecordsBloc` already proves "one bloc per screen-level concern, mediated by the widget layer
when two blocs' worlds touch" is this codebase's established shape; duplicating it for the side menu (instead
of cramming pagination/offline-list state into `ChatBloc` itself, which already owns a materially different
concern — one conversation's live streaming turn) keeps each bloc's test surface focused, exactly like
`RecordsBloc` staying independent of `SessionBloc`/`VaultBloc`. Treating Home/Chat as one persistent,
unparameterized screen that swaps its *content* in place (rather than navigating to a new route per
conversation) matches how the prototype itself describes it ("Tela 1" is one screen with internal states, not
N screens) and avoids inventing a routing concept (a `sessionId`-parameterized chat route) nothing in
`app_router.dart`'s existing five static routes needs elsewhere.

**Alternatives considered**: one combined `ChatBloc` owning both the live conversation and the side-menu list
— rejected, conflates two independently-paginated/independently-failing concerns into one state class, making
every `ChatReady`-consuming test also need to reason about session-list pagination; a bloc-to-bloc import
(`ChatSessionsBloc` emitting an event `ChatBloc` listens to directly) — rejected, same "no BLoC imports another
BLoC directly" shape RF07's own acceptance criterion already establishes as this codebase's convention, even
though the architecture test (`no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`) only mechanically enforces it *across*
features; a new `/home/:sessionId` route — rejected, forces `go_router` to own "which conversation is open,"
duplicating state the bloc already needs to track for the composer-gating/streaming logic regardless.

## R8 — Live offline reactivity vs. the write-path pre-check

**Decision**: two complementary mechanisms, not one:
1. `ConnectivityChecker` (core/network, already used read-only via `hasConnection()`) gains
   `Stream<bool> get onConnectivityChanged`, wrapping `connectivity_plus`'s own `Connectivity
   ().onConnectivityChanged` broadcast stream (mapping "any non-`none` result" → `true`, same predicate
   `hasConnection()` already uses). `ChatBloc` subscribes to it once in its constructor, updating
   `ChatReady.isOffline` live — this is what drives the offline banner and the composer's disabled look
   appearing/disappearing with **zero** user interaction, satisfying SC-006's "re-enabling within one
   interaction of connectivity returning" trivially (zero still satisfies "within one").
2. Independently, every write path (`MessageSubmitted`, `MessageRetryRequested`, and the lazy session-create
   they trigger) still calls `ConnectivityChecker.hasConnection()` synchronously before attempting anything —
   the exact pre-check `SaveTextEntryUseCase` (RF01) already established for every write — so FR-012's "MUST
   be blocked client-side rather than attempted and failed" holds even in the (rare, platform-dependent) case
   where the live stream hasn't yet delivered a transition event.

**Rationale**: every existing write path in this app (`capture/`'s three use cases) already uses the
synchronous pre-check alone, because none of them needed to react to a connectivity change *while the screen
sits idle* — a modal is either opened online or not. Chat's own FR-011 is different: the banner and the
composer's disabled state must track connectivity *continuously* while the screen is simply sitting open, not
only at the moment of an attempted action, so a live stream is a new, genuinely necessary addition (not
duplicated effort) layered on top of the pre-check this app already trusts for the actual gating decision.

**Alternatives considered**: a periodic `Timer.periodic` poll of `hasConnection()` instead of
`connectivity_plus`'s own change stream — rejected, strictly worse (polling delay vs. an OS-level push
notification the package already wraps) for no benefit, and `connectivity_plus` is already a project
dependency; relying on the live stream alone, dropping the synchronous pre-check — rejected, FR-012 asks for a
guarantee ("MUST NOT attempt"), and a stream subscription racing against a fast tap is a weaker guarantee than
a synchronous check immediately before the call.

## R9 — Single-flight-per-conversation gating (FR-007)

**Decision**: `ChatReady` carries one `bool awaitingResponse` (true from the moment a send/retry is dispatched
until that turn's stream reaches `done`/`error`). The composer widget disables itself whenever
`awaitingResponse || isOffline`. No generation counter is needed (unlike `RecordsBloc`'s `_fetchGeneration`):
`RecordsBloc` needs one because *reads* can be superseded by a newer, unrelated read firing before the old one
resolves; here, the composer being disabled while `awaitingResponse` is true means a second
`MessageSubmitted`/`MessageRetryRequested` physically cannot fire for the same conversation until the first
one resolves — there is never a second in-flight write to supersede.

**Rationale**: FR-007 itself states the goal as "a single conversation never has two responses in flight at
once," which disabling the one entry point that could start a second one already guarantees by construction,
simpler than tracking and discarding a superseded response that this design never allows to start.

**Alternatives considered**: reusing a `RecordsBloc`-style generation counter defensively, in case some future
code path bypasses the composer's disabled state — rejected as unneeded defensive complexity; the one
dispatch site for each event lives entirely inside this unit's own two widgets, both of which already read
`awaitingResponse` to decide whether to even allow the tap.

## R10 — Matching a retry's result back to the right message by position, not by assuming id-reuse

**Decision**: `ChatBloc` tracks, per in-flight or just-failed turn, the **index** of the assistant message in
its `messages` list (not just its id) when dispatching `MessageRetryRequested(userMessageId)`. The retry's
eventual `done`/`error` outcome replaces whatever is at that same index with a freshly-constructed
`ChatMessage` — regardless of whether the backend's `message_created` event for the retry returns a brand-new
`assistantMessageId` or (hypothetically) reuses the original failed message's id, since neither OpenAPI nor
`error-taxonomy.md` states which.

**Rationale**: the contract is silent on this specific detail (`chat.messages.retry`'s summary only says "the
original question... rather than a new message pair" — about the *question* not duplicating, not about the
*response*'s id semantics). Matching by list position rather than by asserting a specific id-reuse behavior
means this unit's own logic doesn't accidentally depend on an assumption the backend's actual implementation
might not share; Acceptance Scenario 2 ("the user's original question appears exactly once") is satisfied
regardless, since the question itself is never re-appended on a retry — only the one response slot is ever
replaced.

**Alternatives considered**: asserting the retry's `assistantMessageId` always equals a previous attempt's —
rejected, an unverifiable assumption about backend internals; appending a brand-new response message after the
failed one instead of replacing it in place — rejected, directly contradicts FR-006 ("MUST NOT duplicate the
user's original question... only replaces the failed answer with a new attempt") and Acceptance Scenario 2.

## R11 — A `GET`-sourced `status == 'streaming'` row (Edge Cases: navigating away mid-stream)

**Decision**: when `chat-messages-list` is fetched (on first opening a conversation, or re-opening one after
navigating away) and a returned message's `status` is `streaming` even though this `ChatBloc` instance has no
active SSE subscription for it, it is rendered as a static, non-interactive variant of the streaming bubble —
pulsing-cursor visual, but no token updates ever arrive and it is **not** tappable (it is neither `complete`
nor `failed`, so none of FR-004's two end-state renderings nor FR-006's retry affordance apply to it). No
polling, no reconnect-to-stream attempt is built for this case.

**Rationale**: the Edge Case itself only requires that *returning* to the conversation shows "whatever the
backend ultimately recorded for it (complete or failed)" — by the time a user navigates away and back (even
quickly), the backend-side generation has almost always already finished, since nothing in this unit's design
cancels the backend's own generation just because the app stopped reading its SSE response (closing the local
`dio` stream subscription does not and cannot command the backend to stop). A literal `status: 'streaming'`
read from a fresh `GET` is therefore an exceptionally narrow race (returning within the same second generation
started) that the spec's own wording ("the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded") doesn't
actually require resolving instantly — the next time that conversation is opened or refreshed, the status will
have settled. Building a reconnect/poll mechanism for a transient race nothing in spec.md, the OpenAPI
contract, or the prototype describes would be speculative scope the spec doesn't ask for.

**Alternatives considered**: polling `chat-messages-list` every N seconds while any message shows `streaming`
— rejected as unspecified scope/complexity (no interval is defined anywhere, and it would need its own
start/stop lifecycle tied to screen visibility); treating a `streaming`-status row from `GET` as `failed` —
rejected, actively misleading (it may well complete successfully a moment later, and nothing failed).

## R12 — Client-side message-length handling (Edge Cases: near/at the backend's maximum)

**Decision**: the composer enforces `maxLength: 8000` directly on its `TextField` (the exact value
`chat.messages.send`'s request schema already declares), via Flutter's own `maxLength` property — the OS
keyboard/field simply stops accepting further input past that point, so a `VALIDATION_ERROR` for "too long" is
structurally unreachable from this screen, and no text the user already typed is ever lost (there's nothing to
lose — input beyond the cap was never accepted into the field to begin with).

**Rationale**: Edge Cases' own wording offers two acceptable shapes ("prevents exceeding that maximum before
sending" **or** "surfaces the backend's resulting validation error clearly") — preventing is strictly simpler
than building a distinct inline-error presentation for one specific, fully-avoidable `VALIDATION_ERROR` case,
and `TextField.maxLength` is a built-in Flutter mechanism, not a new dependency or hand-rolled validator.

**Alternatives considered**: no client-side cap, relying on the backend's `VALIDATION_ERROR` response and
showing it as a send-failure banner — rejected as strictly more implementation (a new error-presentation path)
for a worse user experience (typing 8000+ characters only to have the send rejected) than simply not accepting
the 8001st character.

## R13 — Why no extra use-case classes beyond `ChatTitleDeriver`

**Decision**: `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` call `ChatRepository`'s methods directly and own all orchestration
themselves (lazy session creation before the first send, optimistic placeholders, title derivation, retry
position-matching) — the same shape `RecordsBloc` already uses (it depends only on `EntriesRepository`, with
no intervening use-case layer). The one pure, non-trivial piece of logic genuinely independent of any bloc —
`ChatTitleDeriver.derive()` — is pulled out as its own domain entity/function specifically because RNF07
(≥80% domain coverage) needs something directly unit-testable with zero bloc/repository scaffolding, exactly
like `date_range_filter.dart`/`active_filter_chip.dart` (RF06) and `entry_merger.dart` (RF07) already are.

**Rationale**: `capture/`'s use-case classes (`SaveTextEntryUseCase`, etc.) exist because `InsertionModalBloc`
is shared across several structurally different tabs/flows, each needing its own small, independently-testable
"what does Save actually do here" unit; `ChatBloc` has no such multi-flow fan-out — every event it handles
belongs to the one conversation screen's one flow. Introducing a use-case class per event here (e.g.,
`SendChatMessageUseCase`) would wrap a single repository call in an extra indirection layer with no behavior
of its own beyond what the bloc's handler already needs to do inline (append the optimistic placeholder,
subscribe to the stream, update state per event) — exactly the "don't design for hypothetical future
requirements" judgment `RecordsBloc` already made for RF06/RF07's own orchestration.

**Alternatives considered**: a `SendChatMessageUseCase` wrapping `ChatRepository.sendMessage()` purely for
symmetry with `capture/`'s pattern — rejected as an abstraction with no distinct responsibility of its own,
adding a file and a DI registration for no testability gain `ChatBloc`'s own tests don't already get by
mocking `ChatRepository` directly (the same level `RecordsBlocTest` already mocks `EntriesRepository` at).
